summary: First-party Hubei sources establish Suizhou local natural-resources and real-estate-registration custody and identify Tianditu Suizhou as a public map service. Bounded anonymous requests did not verify a public parcel feature service, schema, CRS, stable native parcel ID, or geometry, so no GeoJSON sample is retained and runtime remains held.
queryOutcomes: Separate English and Chinese discovery queries, outcomes, and actual URLs are recorded in city-10056-suizhou.json.

requestOutcomes.outcome: Official Hubei page retrieved in search results. It states that Tianditu Suizhou was launched as Suizhou's public geographic-information map service and describes public map/search functions, but does not expose a parcel-vector endpoint or parcel schema.

Official Hubei page retrieved in search results. It identifies Suizhou's local natural-resources bureau and real-estate registration center and discusses cadastral/registration visualization, but gives no anonymous parcel API, safe parcel ID field, CRS, or geometry response.
TLS negotiation failed with an internal TLS alert during a bounded request. No certificate exception was used.
HTTP 403 Forbidden from nginx. No login, CAPTCHA bypass, credential, private token, or alternate identity was used.
The publicly indexed linked viewer route returned HTTP 403 with an access-restricted page. It was treated as a route limitation, not evidence of citywide cadastral absence.
The local bureau's indexed registration link exposed this public host/port, which returned HTTP 404 from Apache-Coyote. No further endpoint guessing or unsafe registration-field request was made.
Both official host requests timed out within bounded 15-second requests. No TLS verification was disabled.
Official Hubei planning document was identified during discovery and records public geographic-information infrastructure context; it provides no anonymous parcel download endpoint.
